sections.html:
Values come from the Assessor of Property, Room 206, 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Gallatin (615-452-2412). Look for the second floor, right behind the Walmart. Hours are 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays. Tax payments go to the Trustee in Room 107 of that same building (615-452-1260, same hours).

Address changes for tax notices go through the Assessor, because edits to the roll feed the printed bills. After closing, a buyer who wants the notice mailed somewhere else should call 615-452-2412.

Tax sales are not handled at either desk. For those, the Assessor's FAQ points you to the Clerk and Master.

Commuters from Nashville, about 25 miles southwest, fuel this border county. Gallatin has the courthouse offices, and Hendersonville has the largest population. Eight cities in all share the county: those two plus Goodlettsville, Millersville, Mitchellville, Portland, Westmoreland and White House, with several spilling into neighboring counties.

Growth drives sales. The county counted 215,538 residents in July 2025, up 9.8% since April 2020, and 89,138 housing units, 72.0% owned by their occupants. Median value of an owner-occupied home is $393,100 (2020 to 2024) and median gross rent is $1,424. Builders took out 3,045 permits in 2025. At prices like these, even a small change in the tax rate is noticeable on a seller's bill.

sections.h2: How the bill is worked out
sections.html:
Four numbers make up your tax: appraised value, the assessment ratio fixed by state law, the resulting assessed value, and the rate. Residential and farm property is assessed at one quarter of appraised value, commercial and industrial property at 40 percent. Rates are set by the county commission, and each city is free to add one.

The Assessor's calculation page posts the rates below, each applied to every hundred dollars of assessed value:

Property tax rates by jurisdiction
JurisdictionRate per $100 assessed
Sumner County$1.421
Gallatin$0.5295
Goodlettsville$0.5062
Hendersonville$0.5883
Millersville$0.6698
Mitchellville$0.2534
Portland$0.90
Westmoreland$0.83
White House$0.8961

Rates change, so confirm the current year's figures with the Assessor before you rely on them.

sections.h2: Inside a city or outside one
sections.html:
Inside a city, the bill carries the county rate and the city rate together. Gallatin adds $0.5295 to the county's $1.421, and Hendersonville adds $0.5883. A city may also impose special assessments, so ask the city directly.

Houses outside every city pay only the county rate. Keep that in mind when comparing listings, because identical appraisals can still produce different bills.

The first Monday in October is the due date. Pay by February 28 and no interest applies; from March 1 the account is delinquent. The Trustee takes payment these ways:

  • Online at tnpayments.com with Visa or Mastercard
  • By mail, enclosing the top part of the notice
  • In person at Room 107
  • By phone with a Visa or Mastercard
  • At the local banks named on the back of the notice

Card payments cost 2.65 percent plus $1, which goes to the processing company. Paying by check or cash, you can divide the bill into as many as five partial payments, and anything still owed after February collects interest from March 1. You can see whether a bill has been paid by using the online payment link.

Ring the Assessor in the first week of May to reserve a hearing before the Sumner County Board of Equalization, which sits in June. Chatting informally with appraisal staff is an optional first step. Before calling, line up nearby sales and write down any zoning or physical changes to your house.

May 20 is the state calendar date for mailing change notices and filing for exemptions. If the county board does not settle it, the State Board of Equalization takes appeals until August 1 or 45 days after the county board's notice, whichever falls later. A value generally holds between reappraisals, which come every five years, next in 2029. Staff still look at the outside of each property in the years between.

When you call, expect to be asked which parcel you mean and what you think the value should be. Have your address, any recent appraisal, and photos of problems ready. If you have made no changes to the house, your case rests on comparable sales, so pick homes close by, similar in size and age, that sold recently. If something is physically wrong with the property, such as damage or an unfinished addition, say so early, since the January 1 condition of the building is what the roll reflects.

Two programs sit at the Trustee's office: the state relief rebate for elderly owners, disabled owners and disabled former service members, and a freeze covering the county and certain Sumner cities. Freeze applications open each September. Relief applications are accepted once bills are out, with a cutoff 35 days after the February payment date. Owners 65 and over qualify by income, while disabled former service members and their widowed spouses are exempt from the income test. Every participant requalifies annually.

If you are thinking of selling, check how these programs interact with your timeline. A freeze or rebate applies to the owner who lives in the home, so a buyer cannot simply inherit it. The buyer applies on their own once they qualify, and the Trustee can tell you what paperwork they will need.

Make an appointment by phone at 615-452-1260 or through the Trustee's online scheduler.

sections.h2: Other deadlines that can affect a seller
sections.html:
Several dates on the state calendar, which the Assessor publishes, reach most owners:

  • January 1: the assessment date, when ownership and condition are fixed for the tax year
  • March 15: the deadline to apply for greenbelt
  • May 20: change notices are due out, and exemption applications are due
  • September 1: the cutoff for prorating tax on buildings moved, demolished, badly damaged or finished after January 1

Business owners are sent a personal property schedule by February 1 and send it back by March 1. Shutting down a business as well? Ask the Assessor whether your January 1 tangible property is still on the roll.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
Get the parcel's balance from the Trustee in Room 107 and have the title company prorate it on the settlement statement. The roll names whoever owned the property on the January 1 assessment date. A buyer who never receives a bill should call the Trustee and give the Assessor a mailing address.

A sensible order for a seller: confirm the balance with the Trustee a few days before closing, ask the title company to include the proration in the settlement figures, and keep the paid receipt with your closing papers. If you are selling for cash, the same payoff is simply taken from the proceeds at the table. When the house sits inside a city, remember that the city bill and the county bill are separate amounts that both need to be accounted for, and that special assessments from the city may add one more line to check.

faqs.q: What is the Sumner County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is $1.421 per $100 of assessed value, as posted by the Assessor. Gallatin's listing adds $0.5295 and Hendersonville's $0.5883.

faqs.q: When is the next Sumner County reappraisal?
faqs.a: In 2029, since the county reappraises every five years.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sumner County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, with Visa or Mastercard, online or by phone. The processing company charges 2.65 percent plus $1.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Sumner County assessment?
faqs.a: Phone the Assessor at 615-452-2412 during the first week of May to book a hearing with the county board, which meets in June. Collect comparable sales beforehand.

faqs.q: Does Sumner County have a tax freeze?
faqs.a: Yes, for owners 65 or older, covering the county and part of its cities. The Trustee takes applications, which open each September.
